title: Hazelnut meringue layer cake
subtitle: Crisp meringue layers filled with praline buttercream
excerpt: Hazelnut meringue layer cake stacks crisp, nut-speckled meringue discs with a praline buttercream filling. The meringues have a thin crust and a chewy interior once assembled. Making the Italian meringue buttercream requires a sugar thermometer and close attention to the hot syrup stage.
sourceNotes: French meringue and praline tradition documented in classic French patisserie manuals (public domain). Escoffier, Auguste (Le Guide Culinaire, 1903, public domain). Various 20th-century British patisserie manuals (public domain).

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Bake and store the meringue layers in an airtight container for up to 2 days. Make the praline up to 3 days ahead. Assemble on the day of serving.
recipe.temperatureNote: conventional oven for slow meringue drying

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: Conventional oven, 120 degrees Celsius. Fan oven: 105 degrees Celsius. Leave meringues in the switched-off oven for 1 hour after baking.

glossaryTerms.definition: A foam of egg whites and sugar set by heat. French meringue folds in raw caster sugar; Italian meringue pours a hot sugar syrup onto whisking whites, making it more stable and less prone to weeping. For meringue discs baked low and slow, French meringue is standard. All equipment must be grease-free or the whites will not whisk to full volume.

A confection of caramelised sugar and toasted nuts cooled to a hard slab, then ground to a paste or crushed to a coarse powder. Hazelnut praline is made by cooking hazelnuts in caramel until amber, pouring onto an oiled surface to set, then blitzing. The paste is intensely nutty and used to flavour buttercream, fillings, and ganache.

A buttercream made by pouring hot sugar syrup (cooked to 118 to 121 degrees Celsius) onto egg yolks or whites while whisking, then beating in softened butter once the mixture has cooled. The cooked syrup pasteurises the eggs and makes the buttercream stable at room temperature. It is silkier and less sweet than American buttercream.

content.text: This cake has three components built in sequence: the
meringue
discs, the hazelnut
praline
, and the
Italian buttercream
. Read the recipe in full before starting. The meringue discs and praline can be made ahead; the buttercream is made on the day of assembly.
Method
Roasting the hazelnuts

items.prepNote: skin-on; 150 g for meringue, 100 g for praline

content.text: Spread all the hazelnuts on a baking tray and roast at 180 degrees Celsius for 10 to 12 minutes until the skins crack and the nuts are golden inside. Tip onto a clean kitchen towel and rub briskly to remove most of the skins. Weigh out 150 g for the meringue and 100 g for the praline. Allow to cool before grinding the meringue portion.
Pulse the 150 g of cooled roasted hazelnuts in a food processor until finely chopped but not pasty, about 10 short pulses. Set aside.
Making the meringue discs
Heat the oven to 120 degrees Celsius (conventional) or 105 degrees Celsius (fan). Draw three 20 cm circles on baking paper and place ink-side down on two baking trays.

Ensure the bowl and whisk attachment of the stand mixer are completely clean and grease-free. Wipe with a little lemon juice if in doubt. Whisk the egg whites on medium speed until they form soft peaks. Increase to high speed and add the caster sugar one tablespoon at a time, whisking between each addition. Continue until the meringue is thick, very glossy, and holds stiff peaks, about 8 to 10 minutes.

Fold in the finely chopped roasted hazelnuts with a large spatula in as few strokes as possible. Divide the meringue equally among the three circles and spread each to an even disc of about 1 cm thickness.

Bake for 90 minutes until the surface of each disc is dry and very lightly coloured. Turn off the oven and leave the meringues inside with the door slightly open for a further 1 hour. Peel off the baking paper and cool completely on a rack.
Making the praline

Lightly oil a piece of baking paper on a heatproof surface. Place the caster sugar in a small heavy-based saucepan over medium heat. Do not stir; swirl the pan gently as the sugar melts around the edges. Cook until the caramel is a deep amber colour, about 170 degrees Celsius on a sugar thermometer.

Remove from the heat. Quickly tip in the roasted hazelnuts and stir once to coat. Pour immediately onto the oiled baking paper and spread as thinly as possible. Leave to set hard at room temperature, about 20 minutes.

Break the cooled praline into pieces. Reserve a few whole caramelised nuts for decoration. Blitz the rest in the food processor to a coarse powder (for dusting) or continue blitzing to a paste (for the buttercream). The transition from powder to paste takes about 2 to 3 minutes.
Making the Italian meringue buttercream

items.prepNote: softened to room temperature, cut into cubes

content.text: Place the egg yolks in the bowl of the stand mixer and whisk on high speed until pale and thick, about 3 minutes.

Meanwhile, combine the caster sugar and water in a small heavy-based saucepan. Bring to the boil without stirring, then cook until the syrup reaches 118 degrees Celsius on the sugar thermometer. Work quickly but carefully; the syrup is very hot.

With the mixer running on high, pour the hot syrup in a slow, thin, steady stream down the side of the bowl onto the yolks. Avoid pouring directly onto the whisk. Continue whisking until the bowl is cool to the touch and the mixture is thick and pale, about 5 to 8 minutes.

Reduce the mixer to medium speed. Add the softened butter a few cubes at a time, waiting for each addition to be absorbed before adding the next. If the buttercream looks curdled at any point, keep beating; it will come back together. Once all the butter is in, increase speed to high and beat for 2 minutes until silky.
Fold in the praline paste and beat briefly to combine. Taste and adjust the amount of praline to preference. The buttercream should be spreadable but hold its shape.
Assembly

Place the first meringue disc on a serving plate or board. Spread a generous layer of praline buttercream over the surface with a palette knife. The meringue is fragile; work gently from the centre outward.

Set the second meringue disc on top and press down very lightly to level. Spread more buttercream over the second disc, then set the third disc on top. Use the remaining buttercream to cover the top and sides of the cake or leave the sides exposed for a simpler finish.

Dust the top with ground praline powder and arrange the reserved caramelised hazelnuts in a cluster in the centre. Refrigerate for at least 2 hours before slicing so the buttercream firms and holds the layers together. Remove from the refrigerator 20 minutes before serving.

attrs.problem: Meringue weeps or becomes sticky after baking
attrs.avoid: Avoid baking on a humid day or leaving the meringues uncovered in a warm kitchen.
attrs.fix: Store in an airtight container as soon as the discs are cool. Humidity is the enemy of baked meringue; if the kitchen is steamy, keep the container in the coolest, driest spot.

attrs.avoid: Avoid adding butter that is too cold or too warm.
attrs.fix: If the butter is too cold, the mixture will look grainy. If too warm, it will look soupy. In either case, keep beating; the friction of the mixer will bring the temperature and texture back to the correct point within a few minutes.

attrs.avoid: Avoid stirring the syrup once it starts to boil.
attrs.fix: Swirl the pan gently rather than stirring. If crystals form on the sides of the pan, brush them down with a pastry brush dipped in cold water. If the whole batch crystallises, add a tablespoon of water and start again over low heat.

attrs.avoid: Avoid moving the discs while they are still warm.
attrs.fix: Leave the discs on the baking tray until completely cold. Slide a palette knife underneath gently to release from the paper. Cracks in the meringue are hidden by the buttercream once assembled.

content.text: Sugar syrup at 118 degrees Celsius is around three times hotter than boiling water. Pour it in a slow, controlled stream and keep your face and hands well clear. Have a bowl of cold water nearby in case of a splash. Do not rush this step.
